label: GO step late in episode (trial >= ~83) after a rewarded trial, when the policy strongly favors a2
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=0 at GO, prev_reward=1 in 18647/18652), only when the agent is about to choose a2 (action=2 in all but 1 activation; policy logit a1-a2 < -8 for ~97%), and only late in the episode (ep_trial >= 80, essentially none before trial 79; rate jumps after ~82, so it behaves like a time-in-episode clock combined with a confident rewarded-a2 policy). Uses only observed variables: prev_reward, the model own policy logit at GO, and trial index; the upcoming action==2 version (F1 0.85) is weaker than the policy-logit version. Magnitude grows with consecutive rewarded a2 trials (activations ramp within a window across successive rewarded a2 GO steps) and with low value. Does not fire after unrewarded trials, on a1 choices, or on any trial before ~79. Dev: P 0.92 R 0.93 F1 0.93 mass recall 0.98.

issues: Every factual claim held up. All activation is at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 of 380619 each). 18647 of 18652 activations have prev_reward==1. action==2 on 18651 of 18652. Choice is below -8.91 on 81% and below -4.44 on all but 4. There are 0 activations before trial 70 and 99 in trials 70-79. Dev F1 is 0.929 and test F1 is 0.929, matching the reported scores.
The threshold is tuned but robust. ep_trial>=80 gives F1 0.886 and >=85 gives 0.909. choice<-6 gives 0.899. Using action==2 instead of the logit gives 0.855, as claimed.

The 'late in episode' part is better captured by the model's value output than by the trial index. Replacing ep_trial>=83 with value<6.2 raises test F1 from 0.929 to 0.953 (precision 0.943, recall 0.963, mass recall 0.984). At GO, value<6.2 never occurs before trial 70 (0 steps predicted), so the two variables are confounded. Value probably acts as a countdown to the end of the episode. Treat 'episode clock' as interchangeable with 'low predicted value', which fits the 89%-of-mass-in-the-lowest-value-bin observation.

Misses and false positives on the test split look like scattered noise rather than a pattern. 1025 missed steps hold only 1.9% of the activation mass; they are mostly weak activations (0.02-0.35 of max) at window edges or with borderline logits. The 1659 false positives are a2 GO steps after a reward that sit near the thresholds. No systematic class by phase, transition, reward pattern or good state remains.
The magnitude claim (activation rises over consecutive rewarded a2 GO steps) is supported by the example windows but was not fit, as the explanation itself says. This does not overclaim.
